jamie-ai-note-taker.0: The Jamie AI note taker gets searched a lot for a simple reason: it promises meeting notes without the awkward bot. Meet with clients, candidates or patients? Then that promise matters more than any feature list.
jamie-ai-note-taker.2: Jamie is an AI note taker that captures meeting audio on your computer or phone rather than sending a bot into the call. After the meeting it writes notes, detects tasks and identifies speakers, and per Jamie's pricing page it works with "all online platforms" and in-person meetings.
jamie-ai-note-taker.4: Like a person with a recorder, Jamie records the audio playing on your device and your microphone. That is why it works with Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex or a phone call, and why nobody sees a participant called "Jamie" join.
jamie-ai-note-taker.6: On Free, Jamie costs $0; Plus is $24, Pro $46 a month billed yearly and Team $37 per seat per month billed yearly. Enterprise is custom. Annual prices are what the page shows for the main plans, with monthly billing available through a toggle.
jamie-ai-note-taker.9: That 30-minute cap is the real limit. A 45-minute client call gets cut off. Short check-ins or a trial suit the free plan; daily users will need Plus or Pro.
jamie-ai-note-taker.10: Moving from Free to Plus doubles your notes to 20 a month and raises the meeting cap to 2 hours. Pro removes the note cap, allows 5-hour meetings and adds CRM and AI-tool integrations, while Team adds shared workspaces and admin controls.
jamie-ai-note-taker.11: Privacy is Jamie's strongest feature: bot-free capture, EU hosting, GDPR compliance and a stated policy of no model training on your data. ISO 27001 and DORA are listed on its page. SOC 2 Type II? Marked as pending.

jamie-ai-note-taker.13: Yes, in beta. [Jamie's documentation](https://docs.meetjamie.ai/enterprise/users/mobile-app) lists an iOS app on the App Store and a beta Android app on Google Play. Those mobile apps record in-person meetings, show your meetings and tasks, and let you ask questions on the go. Desktop apps capture online meetings on your computer.
jamie-ai-note-taker.14: Because the Android app is a beta, features may lag the iPhone version, so if in-person capture is your main use, test the mobile app on a real meeting before committing. Room noise and distance from the phone affect any tool's accuracy.
jamie-ai-note-taker.15: Reviews on sites such as G2 and Trustpilot tend to praise 3 things about Jamie: no bot, clean summaries, and language coverage. Common complaints? The 30-minute free cap and the price jump to unlimited notes.
jamie-ai-note-taker.16: Jamie, Granola and Otter take 3 different approaches. Two are bot-free (Jamie and Granola), while Otter sends a meeting agent. On price, Granola Business costs $14, Otter Pro costs $8.33 billed yearly, and Jamie's unlimited Pro plan costs $46 a month billed yearly.
jamie-ai-note-taker.18: Which Jamie alternative is best depends on what you are missing. Want a bigger free plan? Fathom records unlimited calls. Cheaper bot-free notes: Granola Business costs $14. And for prep, live answers and follow-up work, Lynkk (our product) costs $15 a month.
jamie-ai-note-taker.20: 17 languages are supported, Hindi and Hinglish included, and teams can pin data to the US, EU, UK, India, Singapore or Australia. On the free plan you get 5 notes a month at up to 2 hours each. Jamie's? 30 minutes.
jamie-ai-note-taker.23: Jamie is worth it if bot-free capture and EU hosting are must-haves, you meet in several languages, and you can justify $46 a month for unlimited notes. Want a generous free plan, US data hosting, or tasks that land in Jira automatically? Then it is less worth it.
jamie-ai-note-taker.24: Yes. Jamie's free plan includes 10 AI notes a month, each up to 30 minutes long, and paid plans start at $24 for Plus. That 30-minute cap is the main limit, so a 45-minute client call gets cut off. Short check-ins and testing suit it better than daily use.
jamie-ai-note-taker.25: Jamie Plus costs $24, Pro costs $46 a month billed yearly, and Team costs $37 per seat per month billed yearly. Enterprise pricing is custom, and monthly billing is available through a toggle on Jamie's pricing page. Pro is the first plan with unlimited notes and 5-hour meetings.
jamie-ai-note-taker.26: No. Jamie records audio from your device, so no bot appears in Zoom, Google Meet or Teams. Attendees still need to be told the meeting is being recorded. Because nothing joins the call, it works with almost any meeting app. The catch: you must start it yourself, so missed starts mean missed notes.
jamie-ai-note-taker.27: Yes, in beta. Jamie offers an iOS app and a beta Android app for in-person meetings, while desktop apps handle online meetings. Because the Android app is a beta, features may lag the iPhone version. Test it on a real in-person meeting before relying on it.
jamie-ai-note-taker.28: Jamie lists notes and transcripts in 99+ languages on its pricing page. Speaker recognition and task detection are included on every plan. Data is hosted in the EU, and Jamie states it does not train models on your data, which suits teams with European clients or strict privacy rules.
